market_name: Will 7 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check 2y and 10y yields and fed funds futures (SOFR strip) for confirming downward move; verify TLT is bid, not idiosyncratic.
time_plan.1h: Confirm whether move is driven by a macro catalyst (data, Fed speak, risk event) or just prediction-market noise; re-check yield curve steepening/flattening.
time_plan.2h: Assess persistence: has TLT held gains or faded? Compare with USD and gold for a coherent dovish signal.
time_plan.6h: Look for any scheduled Fed communication or data release that validates easing expectations; reassess magnitude vs the tiny realistic move.
time_plan.12h: Mark final TLT return vs prediction; note whether the probability shift preceded any public catalyst (leakage test) or reversed.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 7 Fed cuts in 2026 reflects a dramatic dovish repricing — markets pricing ~175bps of easing implies expectations of sharp disinflation or recession/crisis. Falling policy-rate expectations pull down the whole curve, and long-duration Treasuries rally most as forward rate cuts get priced in. TLT is a clean, liquid proxy for that duration bid.

predictions.tradable_instrument_name: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check DXY, EURUSD, USDJPY for confirming dollar weakness; distinguish risk-off haven bid from dovish repricing.
time_plan.1h: Verify whether front-end US rates are leading the FX move; watch for haven flows that would invert the sign.
time_plan.2h: Reassess coherence across TLT, gold and USD — a genuine dovish signal should weaken USD and lift both.
time_plan.6h: Check for any macro data or Fed commentary; gauge whether the FX move is sticky or mean-reverting.
time_plan.12h: Record UUP return vs forecast; flag if the move was already public information or if the proxy proved weakly exposed.

predictions.reasoning: A spike in the odds of 7 cuts implies aggressive Fed easing relative to other central banks, narrowing rate differentials and weakening the dollar. UUP tracks the broad USD and would drift lower on a dovish repricing. Weaker/noisier than the Treasury link because relative central-bank paths matter and a crisis scenario can paradoxically bid USD as a haven.

evidence_used: Market resolves on count of 25bp Fed cuts in 2026, so 7 cuts is an extreme dovish outcome (~175bps easing)
A rising implied probability of 7 cuts signals expectations of sharp easing, typically tied to disinflation or recession/crisis
Standard rate-transmission: lower expected policy path lifts long-duration Treasuries and pressures the USD
Gold and duration are the classic dovish-repricing beneficiaries
uncertainty_notes: The mislabeled 'military_conflict' topic is spurious; this is a monetary-policy market
7 cuts is a tail scenario — probability moves may be noise on a thin, low-probability contract
Recession-driven easing can trigger risk-off USD haven bids that flip the FX sign
12h asset moves from a prediction-market probability shift are realistically tens of bps, far below the 700bps tradable threshold

llm_justification.summary: This market prices the odds of an extremely dovish 2026 Fed path (7 cuts). A sharp rise in that probability signals aggressive easing expectations, which maps most cleanly to a rally in long-duration Treasuries (TLT up) and, more weakly, a softer US dollar (UUP down). Both mappings are directionally sound but the expected 12h magnitudes are small — well under the 700bps tradable bar — so this is a low-conviction, research-only signal.
key_assumptions: A move in this market reflects genuine shifts in Fed easing expectations, not idiosyncratic liquidity
Dovish repricing transmits to lower yields (TLT up) and weaker USD via rate differentials
No offsetting risk-off haven bid overwhelms the rate-differential channel
failure_modes: The 7-cut scenario implies crisis/recession, which can spark risk-off USD strength — flipping the FX call
The probability shift may already reflect public data (jobs, CPI, Fed speak), so no leakage/edge exists
Thin tail-contract moves are noisy and may reverse quickly
TLT and UUP are only broad proxies; a specific curve or cross move may not follow the aggregate
Realistic 12h magnitudes are far below the 700bps tradable threshold, so neither prediction is actionable
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
